newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower ahead of U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower ahead of U.S. jobs data.

text.p: French stocks opened weaker on Friday in cautious trading ahead of the U.S. employment report for December due in the afternoon at 1330 GMT.

Brokers said investors were taking some profits on the bourse's 0.75 percent rise on Thursday that brought it within striking distance of its all-time record of 2,360.98 points after favourable U.S. producer price figures.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 7.24 points, or 0.31 percent, at 2,341.84 at 0910 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was six points lower at 2,345.

Dealers said the poor performance of the Tokyo market, which ended the week at a two-year low after a string of losses, was worrying, but they said the driving influence for the Paris bourse remains the U.S. market.
The top losers on the bourse on Friday were Japanese shares listed in Paris. Mitsubishi Corp.'s stock was down 5.70 francs at 47.40, followed by Sumitomo Bank's stock, down four francs at 64.10.
Shares in French financial group Paribas extended their gains after the group announced the sale on Thursday of its Credit du Nord subsidiary to bank Societe Generale.
Paribas shares rose 0.62 percent to 356.40 francs, adding to Thursday's 4.02 percent gain, as investors applauded the group's strategy to keep selling assets and focus on core businesses.
